weekLabel: Project 1 · Evidence Before Design · Six-Slide Template

slides.title: Replace with one bounded evidence claim
slides.subtitle: Student · dataset · Project 1 pin-up
slides.teaching: Template slide. Replace every prompt; do not add slides.

slides.title: 1 · Question, data, and trustworthiness

left.head: QUESTION
left.body: One answerable architectural question · why it matters · unit of analysis

right.head: DATA EVIDENCE
right.body: Source · what one row means · units · n_rows and n_measured · cleaning decision · one key check

slides.teaching: Show the question and provenance before results.

slides.title: 2 · Group comparison and outlier decision
slides.callout: Show grouped evidence, one checked IQR decision, and a sensitivity check. Missing values and numeric outliers are separate flags.
slides.teaching: Replace the prompts; explain EXCLUDE decisions in the callout rather than squeezing prose into a table cell.

slides.title: 3 · Two static figures answer two questions

left.head: FIGURE 1
left.body: Insert a distribution or group comparison. Label axes and units; add alt text and one finding sentence.

right.head: FIGURE 2
right.body: Insert a relationship or change figure. Annotate the important case and state what it means.

slides.teaching: Use exported PNGs; keep axes, units, and color contrast legible.

slides.title: 4 · One extension: map or animation

left.head: INSERT OUTPUT
left.body:
Map: CRS, operation, legend, and spatial meaning.

Animation: changing variable, fixed conditions, and what motion reveals.

right.head: WHY IT MATTERS
right.body: One finding · one limitation · one sentence explaining how the extension qualifies the static evidence

slides.teaching: Complete one extension only; the six-slide count includes this slide.

slides.title: 5 · Recommendation, limits, and next evidence
takeaways: Replace with the next evidence-gathering step.
slides.teaching: Return to the original question; distinguish evidence from design judgment.
